venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.narrative: **CCATL — Thursday 8/20 (MOD: MKZ)** Net sales $1,912 against a $2,305 target (83%). Food $304, events $0, comps $25.50 (O4W). 64 guests / $29.88 check average. Brutally hot — H98/L80 with heat advisories that thinned Beltline traffic; only 2 meal deals sold all day. Slow start, opener cut at 6:30 with the barback on batch prep. Sharp pivot to higher volume at 7pm — Sargent opened Tuesday across the stairwell, and the team expects more pre-dinner and nightcap traffic now that the O4W neighborhood is fully built out. Volume dipped at 10 with the normal late-night pop at 11 from service-industry friends, plus a lot of late-night food orders. Kitchen: BOH strong; KJ finished his ServSafe certification. Maintenance: 3-comp sink drain fixed. 86 pils, 86 High Life ponies (boilermakers). No incidents; no-shows not charged.

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.narrative: **CCNSH — Thursday 8/20 (MOD: KK, KE, JMS)** Net sales $2,284 against a $1,345 target (170%). Food $139, comps $34.80 (1.5%). 82 guests / $27.85 check average. Slightly nicer out, humid. Decent flow: $580 by 7pm, ~$1,000 by 8:30/9, with the bulk of sales landing after 9pm. Several good groups including a handful of first dates and a table of nurses new to Vandy who loved the Espresso Martini, Wild Strawberry Daiquiri, and gin Adventure Gimlet. Kala safely walked a young guest (too many nicotine pouches, not intoxicated) to an Uber. Kitchen: John-Michael caught up on projects and made killer staff-meal burritos. 86 High Life until tomorrow. Favorite moment: Adrian, a musician new to town, found his new haven and loved the Cast Iron Sour — likely new regular. No incidents; no-shows not charged.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative: **DVR — Thursday 8/20 (AM: Chef Josh & Maggie S; PM: Chef Lucas & Evan F)** DC/AM $1,036.98, D&C PM $12,025.74, Garden/6A $1,608.69; net sales $12,025.74 against a $10,830 target before events — crushed the daily forecast. Add $1,500 net event sales for $13,525.74 total. Food $2,295.10 plus $1,215 event food = $3,510.10. Comps $332.34 (~2.76%). 277 guests (Tock) / $48.83 average. Beautiful August evening. AM: killer steady day with Care Leite running IRDs "out the wazoo." PM: steady and chill until the last hour and a half, then slammed — team pushed last call another 15/30 minutes. Garden solo (Han Solo) for Lucas, dead until sundown. Events: Day 3 of Anaconda LLC meetings, 15 guests 8am-1pm in Vauxhall — productive wrap, host thanked the team. Kitchen slow but great vibes. Maintenance: worn Garden chair logged in Intelity. Jordan's birthday among the night's highlights. No incidents; no-shows not charged.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative: **EV — Thursday 8/20 (MOD: Kyler)** Net sales $5,890 against a $6,200 target (95%). Food $692, beverage $5,044, events $0, comps $195. 134 guests (SevenRooms) / $43.96 check average. Torrential rain right at open (down to 65 at night) with some reservations cancelling; slow start but the room filled by 8:30 — an 11-top from Tromba with a rep splurging on food and drinks for her group filled the heart of the room. 8pm brought a wave of dates and a short waitlist cleared by 10pm. Streets went quiet after 11, but night-capper friend groups revived the bar and midnight filled it completely, pushing sales until 2am. Koba stopped in (in disguise) celebrating the end of jury duty; also Kenan Anderson, regular Braxton, and Seth from Batemans escaping the rain; 4 birthdays celebrated. Breakage: wine glass, egg coupe. Menu count 20. No no-shows, no incidents.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative: **LA — Thursday 8/20 (MOD: Gigi & Oscar)** Net sales $7,384 against a $5,988 target (123%), all Marquee. Food $1,276, events $0, comps $173.32 (DNLs, service recovery, birthday gifts, member discount). 168 guests / $43.95 check average. Muy caliente. Busy right from the start — bar and most tables filled 6-6:30pm, a 9-top took most of Bailey's attention the first hour until Julian arrived. Breaks cleared before the bigger 9pm rush; consistent all night to 10:30. Analise crushed her first live host shift. Julian earned a standout shoutout: a first-time table sent back their first cocktails, loved the off-menu second round, stayed until close, and called it one of the best bar experiences they've ever had. Kitchen: strong — tons of oysters, lamb burgers, and chicken; Oscar crushed it. The back-restroom smell resolved. No incidents; no-shows charged.

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.weather: Hot & humid, tornado warning, downpour, then gorgeous
venues.narrative: **DC — Thursday 8/20 (MOD: Marcus)** Marquee bar sales $3,573.66 plus $6,138 in event sales (Garden event) for $9,711.66 total net against a $5,261 target (185%). Food $284, comps $6.60 (community/investor). 101 guests (62 walk-ins / 39 resos, SevenRooms). Crazy weather — hot and humid to start, a tornado warning and downpour, then gorgeous. Rough start with little traction outside the garden event until ~7:45pm; a wave of two-tops at 8:30 and steady flow to 10:30, though the hoped-for late-night rush never came. Local member Cristiana Piccinni closed the night celebrating her birthday. Kitchen: fantastic across both the garden event and service — incredible plating. Table 34 loved champagne service for Miller High Life. Improvement note: be more proactive/anticipatory. Maintenance: kitchen garbage disposal. No incidents; no-shows not charged.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.narrative: **MG — Thursday 8/20 (AM: Braden & Sam; PM: James & Marcus)** Total net sales $7,606 against a $7,500 target (101%): Municipal Bar AM $1,110 / PM $5,005, Sun Club $282, Hot Eye $1,149. Food $2,644, comps $403. 197 guests (51 AM / 146 PM, OpenTable) / $38.61 average. Hot again. AM: steady 1-4 tables an hour, lots of lattes, PVD bar friends in for cocktails and breakfast. PM: strong early push before the sold-out Indiana Jones screening at the Lucas; volume declined after 7 when the movie began but never fully emptied, and the late-night pop was easy to handle. Sun Club steady; lowboy door suction failing. Hot Eye picked up at 9:30 with larger groups and a big industry crowd — Alexis received her first Death & Co member card from a local couple. Kitchen: Raiders drove some business; no lows or 86s; a dozen oysters comped at one table (kitchen thought they were fine). Favorite moment: member Marlene giddily using her new physical D&C card for the first time. No incidents.
